title: Lute compiled execution IR (irVersion 0.38.x)
description:
JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) for the WHOLE compiled Lute IR artifact emitted by `lute compile` (crates/lute-compile, ir.rs `ExecutionIr`). One artifact is produced per `.lute` document; a project's engine unions the per-document `relations`/`rules`/`seedFacts`/`entities`/`enums`/`prereqEdges` across every artifact exactly as it unions the command streams.

VERSION-NEGOTIATION POLICY (docs/runtime/execution-model.md, Version negotiation): before 1.0 an engine gates on the exact `irVersion` MAJOR.MINOR line it implements — an engine for 0.38.x accepts only 0.38.* artifacts and refuses every other line (E-ENGINE-IR-VERSION), because pre-1.0 minors may change the IR shape (clean cutover, D6). Patch levels within the line are compatible. Unknown fields within a known kind are ignored; an unknown command `kind` is a hard error. From 1.0 the gate becomes MAJOR only.

IR 0.38.0 (dsl 0.38.0 §5) is a clean cutover with no legacy aliases: the envelope stamp is `capabilitySnapshot`; the descriptive heading table is `sections`; every command record carries required `kind`, `family` (the normative kind grouping a runtime dispatches on before `kind`), and `position`; per-record timing lives only in the nested `timing` object; staging kinds are `bg`, `music`, `sfx`, `vfx`, `actor`, `camera`, `cg`, `video`, and `sequence`. A runtime reads timing only from `timing` and never from flattened legacy fields.

kind.description: document kind discriminator (dsl 0.2.0 §2/§3.1; `lore` since dsl 0.19.0 §2); read first — it selects `meta`'s shape.

lute.description: language-version pin (informational for the runtime), e.g. "0.7.0".

irVersion.description: IR schema version the engine gates on: the exact MAJOR.MINOR line before 1.0, MAJOR only from 1.0, e.g. "0.38.0".

capabilitySnapshot.description: plugin-system §13 capability snapshot stamp (`snapshot.version`, a content hash); a consumer may refuse a mismatched snapshot. dsl 0.37.0 §5.3: no `capabilityVersion` alias is emitted.

to.description: the canonical NodeKey that replaces it.

identityRenames.description: OPTIONAL authored save-identity migrations from `lute.project.yaml` relevant to this artifact, sorted by `from`; omitted when empty. Engines apply them when loading save-shaped identity and MUST NOT infer renames from position, text, or spans. `project.index.json` exposes the same list.

requiredSemantics.description: compiler-derived, sorted semantic capability ids required by this artifact.

state.description: the folded init/type table (§4.1); may be empty but is always present.

entities.description: merged relational entity kinds; omitted entirely when empty.

enums.description: merged relational enums; omitted when empty.

relations.description: merged relation declarations; omitted when empty.

seedFacts.description: merged seed facts (vocabulary order); omitted when empty.

rules.description: merged Datalog rules as DATA (vocabulary order); omitted when empty. Lute runs no fixpoint (D1).

commands.description: the flat command-record stream (§4.4; record shapes dsl 0.37.0 §5.3), in execution order.

prereqEdges.description: advisory raw `after` / `follows` graph edges (connectivity T13); omitted when empty.

sections.description: dsl 0.37.0 §5.3: authored `## ` document sections, in document order — each with its one-based `section` number, verbatim heading text, and optional stable `{#id}`. Emitted only for sections with a non-empty heading or an id; omitted entirely when none qualifies. Purely descriptive: control flow never references it; the first segment of a record `position` is the section number.

clock.description: dsl 0.24.0 §1: the declared clock the document was compiled against. Omitted when the project declares none. Serialized after `sections`.

gates.description: dsl 0.27.0 §4 (T2-3): every occasion's declared `raisedWhen` gate, occasion-sorted, `@def`-expanded. The engine raises the occasion only while its gate holds; `occasion.target` in it reads the member the occasion is raised for (`room.office` → `office`). A clock raise (`raise.slot` / `dayStart` / `dayEnd`) whose gate is false is not made. Omitted when no occasion declares one; serialized after `clock`.

terminal.description: dsl 0.27.0 §4 (T2-4): the project's `terminal:` condition (declared by a schema; several joined by `||`), `@def`-expanded. Once it holds the game is over: the engine raises no occasion and the clock does not advance until a new run. Omitted without one; serialized after `gates`.

terminalPersists.description: dsl 0.29.0: every `terminal:` declaration is the long form with `persists: true` — the ending outlives runs on purpose, so a new run does not reopen the game. Omitted when false; serialized after `terminal`.

seasons.description: dsl 0.27.0 §5: the declared seasons, name-sorted, each with its `@def`-expanded `live` condition. When `live` goes false→true the engine opens the season: `season.<name>.*` back to the declared defaults (the old values to `prev.season.<name>.*`), its `once: season:<name>` beats and `tier: season:<name>` quests reset. Omitted when none; serialized after `clock`, `gates` and `terminal`.

outsideRun.description: dsl 0.28.0 (T2-9): the occasions declared `outsideRun: true`, name-sorted. The engine raises these even after `terminal` holds (a title screen, a gallery between runs); every other occasion stays closed once the game is over. Omitted when none; serialized after `seasons`.

celEnv.description: dsl 0.32.0 §1.4 / §7: the CEL environment (variables and host function signatures) expressions were checked against.

by.description: the named injection rule responsible, e.g. "auto-anchor-on-show".

explanation.description: human-readable justification, authored by the COMPILER in English for a human reader. Renamed from `reason` in IR 0.10.0 (#36): `end.reason` on the `end` command is an opaque author-written token a host dispatches on, and the two share no contract — `explanation` cannot be read as a dispatch key.

provenance.description: §4.3 injection provenance (lute_check::inject::Provenance): why a compiler-injected record exists. Present only on injected records; its presence is the injection marker (IR 0.37.0 drops the constant `injected` flag).

source.description: §4.3 component source stamp on component-expanded records (D8).

position.description: a resolved record position (dsl 0.37.0 §5.3), unique within the artifact; its first segment is the one-based section number. Build-local execution ordering only — never an identity. Fields that carry a position: every command `position`; `choice.converge`/`options[].target`; `hub.converge`/`return`/`options[].target`; `match.converge`/`otherwise`/`arms[].target`; `jump.target`; `quest.objectives[].body`; `on.body`; `entry.body`; `beat.body`.

family.description: dsl 0.37.0 §5.1: the normative grouping of a record's `kind`, read by runtime dispatch before `kind`. content: line; staging: bg, music, sfx, vfx, actor, camera, cg, video, sequence; state: set, assert, retract; control: choice, match, hub, jump, end, barrier; declaration: quest, on, entry, accept, beat; plugin: plugin.

wait.description: resolved blocking flag: when true the engine finishes presenting the record before advancing.

at.description: scheduled placement in seconds (finite, >= 0) within the record's timeline.

timeline.description: zero-based ordinal of the `<timeline>` the record was emitted from — an ordinal, not seconds. Present only for records emitted from a timeline.

timing.description: dsl 0.37.0 §5.2: a record's resolved timing, replacing the flattened 0.36 stamp fields. Omitted when every member is absent; each member is omitted when absent. A runtime reads timing only from here.

segment.description: dsl 0.37.0 §3.6: one presentation segment of a modified line — a coalesced text run or a pause leaf.

text.description: plain derived text of the run (escapes decoded, `{{…}}` markers verbatim); empty runs are omitted.

styles.description: active project `textStyle` members, outermost first. Omitted when none.

rate.description: active `speed` rate (the innermost one when nested). Omitted when none.

exprNode.description: Portable CEL expression AST (dsl 0.32.0 §7, expr.rs). Serialized as an UNTAGGED serde enum — each variant is a bare object distinguished by its keys. A plain JSON walker evaluates it; the parallel `cel` string field carries the standard CEL expression.

int.description: 64-bit signed integer literal, constrained to ±2^53 for exact JSON representation.

call.description: function name: int, double, holds, count, countDistinct, validAt, now, visited, etc.

oneOf.description: function call: int(), double(), or host function.

cel.description: standard CEL expression text after @def/$/is= expansion.

authored.description: source text when it differs from cel (e.g. authored shorthand or unexpanded text).

celSlot.description: dsl 0.32.0 §7: CEL slot object carrying standard CEL expression text, lowered portable expr AST, and optional authored source text.

variables.description: Environment variables checked against, e.g. root state namespaces typed as map(string, dyn).

functions.description: Host functions called by expressions with their overload signatures.

celEnv.description: dsl 0.32.0 §1.4 / §7: the CEL environment (variables and host function signatures) expressions were checked against.

placeholder.description: One {{…}} interpolation placeholder (IR A3), internally tagged on `kind` (lowercase). The runtime substitutes it against live state; the enclosing `text` keeps the verbatim {{…}} marker.

expr.description: The referenced def body, inlined at compile time (the artifact has no defs table). The engine renders the placeholder by evaluating it like any other CEL slot. Always emitted by lute 0.21.1+ compilers; optional so 0.21.0 artifacts stay valid.

format.description: A text hint (`capitalize`, `start`, `indefinite`) on the rendered token.

oneOf.description: dsl 0.26.0 §5: {{occasion.target}} in a beat or entry targeting a kind (or, dsl 0.27.0 §3, presented once per member with `forKind`) — the member the beat runs for (the beat's `occasion.target`), a member of `entityKind`. Render the member's display name: the `labels[member]` of the `entities[]` entry named `entityKind`, else its cast `name:` when the member is a cast id, else the id.

format.description: A text hint (`capitalize`, `start`, `indefinite`) on the rendered member: `start` / `indefinite` render the `labelForms[member]` form of the `entities[]` entry named `entityKind` when it declares one.

placeholderFormat.description: dsl 0.24.0 §4 / 0.25.0 §8 / 0.27.0 §7: the interpolation's format hint ({{user.deaths:ordinal}}), omitted when none was written. The engine renders the value in that format (a locale-aware engine localizes it). `ordinal`: a non-negative integer as an English ordinal (1st 2nd 3rd 4th … 11th 12th 13th … 21st 22nd … 101st 111th). `ordinalWord`: an ordinal word (first second … twentieth for 1–20, the `ordinal` digits above). `cardinalWord`: a cardinal word (one two … twenty for 1–20, the digits otherwise). `plural`: the placeholder's `forms` — the first when the number is 1, the second otherwise, with `#word` replaced by the number as a cardinal word, `#Word` by that word capitalized and any other `#` by the number. The text hints apply to the text the value renders as (a label, a cast name, a string): `capitalize` upper-cases its first letter; `start` renders the member's declared `labelForms` `start` form, else `capitalize`; `indefinite` renders the declared `indefinite` form, else `an` (before a vowel) or `a`, a space and the text. Any other value renders unchanged.

labelForms.description: member → the label forms a kind's `labels:` entry declares beside its text (`{ text, start, indefinite }`): `start` is what a `:start` placeholder renders, `indefinite` what an `:indefinite` one renders. Omitted when no member declares a form; an absent form falls back (see `placeholderFormat`).

placeholderForms.description: dsl 0.27.0 §7: a `plural` placeholder's forms as written in {{n:plural(lantern|lanterns)}} — the English singular, then the plural; a `#` in a form stands for the number. Present exactly when `format` is `plural`; an engine may localize the count from them.

role.description: dsl 0.37.0 D6: the line's authored delivery role. Every role carries a `voiceKey` — a key is a join, not a recording obligation.

members.description: closed member set; ABSENT for `open: engine` kinds (the engine mints members).

labels.description: dsl 0.27.0 §7: member → display text (the kind's `labels:`, with its sub-kinds' and ancestors' labels for shared members). What a {{…}} of a value of this kind renders — an `occasionTarget` placeholder of this `entityKind` (over a cast `name:`); a `{ domain: <kind> }` state path carries the same map as `state[].labels`. Omitted when none; an unlabelled member renders its id.

tier.description: effective write tier for base relations (default `run`): `scene`, `run`, `user`, `app`, `quest`, or `season:<name>` — the relation's facts go back to the seed facts each time that declared season opens. ABSENT for `derive: true` (a derived relation has no write tier).

key.description: 0-based functional-key arg indices (§4); absent when undeclared.

excludes.description: dsl 0.25.0 §1: relations that never hold together with this one on the same arguments — the symmetric closure of `excludes:`, sorted; absent when none.

args.description: ground literals as strings; bools as "true"/"false". Never "_".

termEntry.description: One rule term (dsl 0.3.0 §7.1), tagged on `kind`. Bools lower to a Const with value "true"/"false".

atomEntry.description: One rule atom: a relation applied to terms (dsl 0.3.0 §7.1).

bodyEntry.description: One rule body literal (dsl 0.3.0 §7.1), tagged on `kind`: a positive/negated atom, a CEL guard, or a term comparison.

oneOf.description: dsl 0.26.0 §6: `count(atom) op n`, or with `distinct` `countDistinct(atom, V…) op n`. A variable of `atom` bound by another literal is read; any other ranges over the facts. `atom`'s relation sits in a strictly lower stratum than the head.

raw.description: the rule's original source text, for engine diagnostics.

ruleEntry.description: One Datalog rule (dsl 0.3.0 §7.1), emitted as STRUCTURED data. Lute performs NO evaluation (D1); the engine runs the least-fixpoint over this rule set.

node.description: the contributing node's canonical key: a scene's {character}.{episodeId}, a quest's <quest id>, or (dsl 0.25.0 §3) a bundle beat's `<document id>.<beat id>`.

after.description: a scene's `after:` or a bundle beat's `after=`: the RAW declared prerequisite formula text — unresolved, unvalidated CEL. An eligibility gate.

follows.description: a quest's `follows=`: the RAW declared quest-graph formula text — unresolved, unvalidated CEL. Graph metadata only; it never gates the quest (its `start` does).

formula.description: the parsed `after` formula, so a runtime never parses `after` text. Present only on an `after` edge whose text is inside the restricted prerequisite profile; absent on `follows` edges.

prereqEdgeEntry.description: One advisory graph edge (connectivity spec §2.6, T13): a single node's raw declared `after` (scene, bundle beat) or `follows` (quest), verbatim.

prereqFormula.description: A parsed `after` prerequisite formula: `visited("id")` / `completed("q")` / `active("q")` atoms joined by `&&` (`and`) / `||` (`or`), each binary node a two-element array [left, right].

id.description: dsl 0.15.0 §2: the resolved canonical scene key — authored `id:` verbatim, else the derived `{character}.{episodeId}` join. Always present on a scene artifact. Character set: [A-Za-z0-9_.-]+, non-empty. This is the identity every consumer (lineId prefix, prereqEdges[].node, project.index.json document key, connectivity visited() targets) joins on.

character.description: dsl 0.15.0 §2: OPTIONAL. On a document that authors `id:`, only the legacy identity keys the author WROTE survive into the artifact (a project-level defaults: fallback SHOULD NOT resurrect a dropped key). On the derived-key path (no `id:` authored), this field is present and resolved as in 0.14.0.

episodeId.description: See sceneMeta.character — OPTIONAL under dsl 0.15.0 §2. On the derived-key path this is the resolved value (authored episodeId verbatim, else `s{season:02}ep{episode:02}`), exactly as in 0.14.0.

extra.description: dsl 0.15.0 §3: free descriptive open mapping the checker admitted past E-META-VALUE. Values are scalars (string / integer / number / boolean) or FLAT sequences of scalars. Never consulted by any checker/compiler/runtime rule and never routed through CEL — the sanctioned home for team search metadata (`arc`, `location`, `tags`, whatever). Key-sorted by the compiler; absent when the document authors no `extra:` block.

plugin.description: plugin-system 0.0.4 §2: checker-validated, plugin-owned top-level frontmatter keys, key -> JSON value (any shape the declaring plugin's frontmatter schema admits, plugin-system 0.0.1 §6.8). Absent when the document authors no plugin-owned key.

beat.description: dsl 0.21.0 §3.1: the scene's beat declaration — present only when the frontmatter names an occasion (`on:`). Absent on a scene that answers no occasion, which is reached by explicit flow as before (docs/runtime/beats-and-occasions.md).

sceneMeta.description: Scene-kind envelope meta (dsl 0.15.0 §2/§3). Present when `kind` == "scene". Since 0.15.0 only `id` is required — the four legacy identity keys demote to optional.

targetKind.description: dsl 0.26.0 §5: a `target: "kind:<kind>"` beat, resolved. It answers a raise for `<prefix>.<member>` of every listed member; while it runs, `occasion.target` is the raised member id.

forKind.description: dsl 0.27.0 §3 (T2-10): a `for: "kind:<kind>"` beat on an untargeted `select: sequence` occasion, resolved. Each raise presents the beat once per listed member whose `when` holds (judged at the raise with `occasion.target` bound to that member), in list order; while one presentation runs, `occasion.target` is that member id. `once` spends the beat, not a member.

on.description: the occasion this scene answers — engine vocabulary, shape-only unless a resolved plugin declares `occasions:` (dsl 0.21.0 §2).

target.description: the scene is a candidate only when the occasion is raised for this target (dotted id, the cmdEntry.target shape). Absent when the beat answers the occasion for any target.

when.description: eligibility condition, `@def`-expanded; the beat is eligible only while this (and the scene's `after:`) holds. Absent when not authored.

once.description: repetition policy: `run` (default — presented at most once per run), `user` (at most once ever), `none` (repeatable; source `once: false`), `day` / `slot` (dsl 0.24.0 §1: spent until the declared clock's day / slot changes — the artifact's `clock` names the paths), `week` (dsl 0.27.0 §5: spent until `clock.weekday` returns to `week.first`), `season:<name>` (dsl 0.27.0 §5: spent until the season opens again). A beat with `spentBy` is `none`.

also.description: dsl 0.23.0 §3: on a `select: first` occasion, an eligible `also` beat is presented in addition to the winner, after it; it never wins. Absent when not authored.

spentBy.description: dsl 0.27.0 §5: the beat (`once: none`) stays eligible until this `@def`-expanded condition holds. Absent when not authored.

share.description: dsl 0.25.0 §2: the shared-spend key. Beats with the same key (project-wide; scene, entry, and bundle beats alike) are spent together: once one is presented (an entry: read), every beat of the key is spent for their common `once` period. Absent when not authored.

advances.description: dsl 0.31.0 §1: clock movement performed when the beat is presented.

sceneBeat.description: A scene beat (dsl 0.21.0 §3.1; docs/runtime/beats-and-occasions.md): the occasion the scene answers and how it competes with the other candidates when the engine raises it.

id.description: dsl 0.19.0 §2.1: the quest document's authored `id:` verbatim (same shape as a scene `id:`). The document's ProjectIndex key. Absent when not authored, so a quest document without `id:` is byte-identical to 0.18.

extra.description: dsl 0.15.0 §3: same descriptive block as sceneMeta.extra, sanctioned on quest roots too. Same scalar / flat-scalar-array shape; key-sorted; absent when the document authors no `extra:` block.

plugin.description: plugin-system 0.0.4 §2: checker-validated, plugin-owned top-level frontmatter keys, key -> JSON value. Absent when the document authors no plugin-owned key.

questMeta.description: Quest-kind envelope meta (dsl 0.2.0 §6.1, dsl 0.15.0 §3, dsl 0.19.0 §2.1). MAY serialize as {} when none of id/title/contentLang/extra/plugin are authored. Present when `kind` == "quest".

domain.description: enum member domain; an implicit branch/quest-state slot appends "unset".

default.description: initial value (any JSON scalar/array/object), integral-collapsed. Absent when the slot has no default (maybe-unset).

owner.description: dsl 0.22.0 §1.2: the engine writes this state path; omitted for content-owned paths.

provenance.description: "branch:<id>" for an implicit choice slot, "quest:<id>" for a reserved quest slot; absent for an author-declared slot.

labels.description: dsl 0.24.0 §1: value -> display label, from the named enum the path is typed against (`{ domain: <name> }`). A `{{path}}` interpolation renders the label when the value has one, the value otherwise. Absent when the enum declares no labels.

stateEntry.description: One folded state slot (§4.1): the engine's init/type table entry.

effectSource.description: The origin of an Effect's value (IR A12, untagged).

bridgeResult.description: read the named key off the bridge call's returned result object.

anyOf.description: a bare literal value (manifest scalar), integral-collapsed.

path.description: fully-resolved dotted state path (scope + segments, fromAttr already substituted at compile time).

effect.description: A resolved plugin state-write binding (IR A12): where a bridge result / increment / literal lands. The runtime applies it after the bridge call — no manifest lookup, no per-plugin knowledge.

text.description: displayed option text (source language; `{{…}}` markers verbatim).

when.description: guard CEL slot; present only when the option is guarded.

texts.description: dsl 0.8.0 §7: merged locale texts, locale tag → translated option text, keyed on `lineId`. Absent when no locale bundle was merged. The source-language string stays in `text`.

text.description: displayed option text (source language; `{{…}}` markers verbatim).

exit.description: leaves the hub loop when taken.

when.description: guard CEL slot; present only when the option is guarded.

texts.description: dsl 0.8.0 §7: merged locale texts, locale tag → translated option text, keyed on `lineId`. Absent when no locale bundle was merged. The source-language string stays in `text`.

hubOption.description: One <hub> option: a choice option plus always-present once/exit revisit flags.

is.description: dsl 0.32.0 §7: authored `is=` shorthand, semantic rather than diagnostic. Absent on `test=` arms.

id.description: dsl 0.37.0 D10: the authored `<reward id>`, unique within its owning quest; the stable model key when present. Omitted when unauthored (the owner-local declaration index is the fallback key).

kind.description: The reward kind id (dsl 0.16.0 §2). When a plugin publishes a `rewardKinds:` vocabulary (§4), the checker's `E-REWARD-KIND` closure gates this against the merged vocabulary; without a vocabulary, any non-empty string is accepted (shape-only mode).

target.description: Optional target id — the address of the effect target (e.g. an inventory owner). Its id-space is pinned by the reward-kind's `target: { provider: <name> }` declaration when the vocabulary declares one; a shape-only kind admits any target string.

amount.description: Scalar amount (dsl 0.16.0 §2, integers, negatives legal). Present when the authored `amount` was a scalar, or when the attribute was unauthored (defaults to `1` per Global Constraints amount defaulting). Mutually exclusive with `amountMin`/`amountMax`.

amountMin.description: Lower bound of a range amount (dsl 0.16.0 §2, `N..M`, `N <= M`). Carried verbatim from the authored value — a reference engine NEVER pre-rolls a value into `amount` (spec D-C); the engine's own dice draw over `[amountMin, amountMax]` at grant time is engine policy the IR does not fix. Present iff `amountMax` is present; both are mutually exclusive with `amount`.

amountMax.description: Upper bound of a range amount — see `amountMin` for the range contract.

when.description: Optional CEL gate evaluated at the grant instant (spec §3). Grants fire iff `when` decides Bool(true); a `false`/`unknown` gate silently skips the entry once (a transition is monotone and fires at most once, so `when` is a one-shot filter, not a re-triable predicate).

outcome.description: Optional lifecycle-transition filter (dsl 0.16.0 §2). Only ever `"failed"` on the wire, and only on a quest-level entry — a quest reward with `outcome="failed"` grants ONLY on a fresh `failed` transition (authored `fail` OR §2.3 cascade); absent `outcome=` means the reward grants ONLY on a fresh `complete`. Objective-level entries never carry `outcome=` (checker `E-REWARD-ATTR`).

credits.description: dsl 0.23.0 §8: the state path the reward kind's `rewardKinds.credits` declares, stamped at compile from the capability snapshot. A grant adds its `amount` to this path (a range amount is the engine's roll; the reference runner credits scalar amounts only). Omitted when the kind credits nothing.

rewardEntry.description: One `<reward id= kind= target= amount= when= outcome=/>` declaration (dsl 0.16.0 §2/§3). Pure data — the compiler NEVER synthesizes handler bodies or `Command::Set` records for a reward; the reference engine (`crates/lute-cli/src/runner.rs` `Runner::emit_grants`) emits deterministic `grant` transcript events at each fresh lifecycle transition, and `lute trace` mirrors those events (`crates/lute-trace/src/walk.rs`).

visibleWhen.description: visibility only: the objective is shown only while this holds. It never gates `done` (authored `visibleWhen=`). Absent when not authored.

body.description: position of the objective's completion-body segment; ALWAYS present, `null` when the body is empty.

quest.description: Referenced child quest id of a subquest objective (<objective quest=...>, language 0.14.0); the objective's done is the synthesized quest.<child>.state == 'complete'. Omitted for authored-done objectives.

rewards.description: dsl 0.16.0 §2/§3 declarative rewards — direct-child `<reward/>` entries of this objective in declaration order. Objective grants fire once at fresh `done` (spec §3 D-D), BEFORE any quest-level grant. `outcome=` is never legal on an objective-level entry (checker `E-REWARD-ATTR`); every entry here has no `outcome` field. Omitted when the objective authors no rewards (byte-identical to 0.15.1 for pre-rewards artifacts).

on.description: dsl 0.21.0 §7a.2: the occasion at which this objective is judged. The engine evaluates the objective's `done` only when it raises this occasion while the quest is `active`, never continuously (docs/runtime/quest-lifecycle.md). Absent when not authored: the objective is evaluated continuously, as before.

by.description: dsl 0.23.0 §2, 0.24.0 §2.1: while the objective is not done, the first time this condition is true the objective FAILS (a required objective fails its quest; `quest.<id>.failedBy` = `by`). Judged at every lifecycle settle, `on` or not — a deadline is a moment, not a place; `done` wins a tie in the same settle. Absent when not authored.

target.description: dsl 0.23.0 §2: with `on`, the objective is judged only when the occasion is raised for this target (the beat target rule). Absent when not authored: judged whenever the occasion is raised, for any target.

until.description: dsl 0.24.0 §2.1: the place-bound deadline (the checker requires `on`). Judged only when the objective's `on` occasion is raised (for `target`, when present) while the quest is `active`, after its `done`; the first time it is true there the objective FAILS (a required objective fails its quest; `quest.<id>.failedBy` = `until`). Absent when not authored.

objectiveEntry.description: One objective inlined in QuestCmd.objectives (dsl 0.2.0 §6.4). Declaration data only; the engine derives completion (all non-optional objectives done ⇒ quest complete).

text.description: source-language plain text: inline modifier delimiters and attrs removed, escapes decoded, `{{…}}` markers verbatim (dsl 0.37.0 §3.6).

voiceKey.description: the voice asset join (dsl 0.37.0 D6); present on every line, any role.

texts.description: dsl 0.8.0 §7, 0.37.0 §6: merged locale texts, locale tag → plain derived text, keyed on `lineId`; every translated locale appears here, modified or not. Absent when no locale bundle was merged. The source-language string stays in `text`.

segments.description: dsl 0.37.0 §3.6: present only when the source line uses an inline modifier — coalesced text runs and pause leaves whose texts concatenate to `text`. Absent on an unmodified line.

localeSegments.description: dsl 0.37.0 §6: for a modified line, locale tag → that translation's segments; every key also appears in `texts`. Absent on an unmodified line or without a locale bundle.

cmdLine.description: A spoken or narrated content line (dsl 0.37.0 §5.3).

cmdBg.description: `::bg` (dsl 0.37.0 §5.3): sets the stage backdrop. Every field optional.

playback.description: project `musicPlayback` domain member (e.g. play/stop). Omitted when unauthored.

exit.description: true when the action is declared in the `action` domain's `exits` (the character leaves the stage); omitted when false or unknown.

emotion.description: stage emotion update, as a line `emotion`.

costume.description: authored costume id; emitted when supplied.

cmdActor.description: `::actor` (dsl 0.37.0 §5.1/§5.3): an authored actor record or a compiler-injected one (anchor, preload, position reset, hide — §7.4). Injected records carry `provenance`; `posReset` and `preload` appear only on injected records.

cmdCamera.description: `::camera` (dsl 0.37.0 D1, §5.3): opaque project-domain members; at least one is present after checking. No numeric transform is synthesized.

display.description: resolved display member (`show` when unauthored); always present.
resolved display member (`show` when unauthored); always present.

cmdSequence.description: `::sequence{name}` (dsl 0.37.0 D3, §5.3): a reference to a project-declared external cinematic. Carries only its name and resolved `timing` (`wait` defaults to true); no bound characters. The reference runner records it without simulating the sequence.

value.description: RHS CEL slot with standard text and portable expression.

cmdAssert.description: One asserted fact delta (dsl 0.3.0 §5). DATA only — the engine applies it as a positive write to the relation's fact set.

cmdRetract.description: One retracted fact delta (dsl 0.3.0 §5). The engine applies it as a negative write; "_" positions are a bulk wildcard the engine resolves.

selectionKey.description: the stable selection-history key a runtime records the chosen option under.

converge.description: position every option segment continues at.

prompt.description: dsl 0.11.0: the choice-situation sentence shown by the UI. Present only when authored.

timeout.description: dsl 0.11.0, 0.37.0 §5.3: the countdown in whole seconds before the branch times out. Present only when authored.

cmdChoice.description: `<choice>` (dsl 0.37.0 §5.3): a player selection; each option's segment is followed by `converge`.

subject.description: the authored `subject` CEL slot; absent when unauthored.

otherwise.description: position of the fallback segment; absent when unauthored.

cmdMatch.description: `<match>` (dsl 0.37.0 §5.3): the first arm whose test holds runs; otherwise `otherwise`, then `converge`.

selectionKey.description: the stable selection-history key a runtime records chosen options under.

prompt.description: dsl 0.23.0 §4: the prompt line shown with the hub's options. Present only when authored.

return.description: dsl 0.28.0 §5: position of the hub's `<return>` segment. It runs each time a non-exit option's segment ends, before the hub is judged and presented again; like an option target it bounds the segment before it. Present only when authored.

cmdHub.description: <hub> (§7.3.2): a choice plus revisit semantics; re-presentation is a runtime property of the hub kind (no backward jump emitted).

cmdJump.description: Unconditional control-flow jump. Carries no `timing`, `provenance`, or `source`.

reason.description: free-form author string the host MAY surface (e.g. "completed"); Lute assigns it no meaning.

cmdEnd.description: dsl 0.8.0 §3: terminate the walk at this record. Equivalent to falling off the end of `commands`, except `reason` is carried.

timeline.description: zero-based ordinal of the timeline this barrier joins (an ordinal, not seconds).

at.description: the join time in seconds (authored duration, else the maximum resolved clip end).

cmdBarrier.description: A timeline join point (dsl 0.37.0 §5.2). Carries no `timing`: its join fields are direct, so they cannot collide with a record's timing. The reference runner records it as a join and simulates no elapsed time.

rewards.description: dsl 0.16.0 §2/§3 declarative rewards — direct-child `<reward/>` entries of this quest in declaration order. Quest grants fire at fresh `complete`/`failed` transitions (spec §3 D-D). A `<reward outcome="failed"/>` entry fires ONLY on `failed` (authored fail OR §2.3 downward cascade); a default (no `outcome=`) entry fires ONLY on `complete`. Runs BEFORE the corresponding `questComplete`/`questFailed` handler bodies. Omitted when the quest authors no rewards (byte-identical to 0.15.1 for pre-rewards artifacts).

rearm.description: dsl 0.27.0 §5: when this `@def`-expanded condition goes from false to true the quest returns to `unset` (objectives undone, `failedBy` cleared) and can be activated again. Omitted when not authored.

tier.description: dsl 0.27.0 §5: `season:<name>` resets the quest to `unset` when that season opens. dsl 0.22.0 §7: `run` for a `<quest tier="run">` — its status and objectives reset to `unset` when a run starts (`newRun`). Omitted for the default `user` tier (status persists across runs).

activate.description: dsl 0.24.0 §2: `accept` for a `<quest activate="accept">` subquest child — it does not activate with its parent; an accept activates it while the parent is `active`. Omitted by default (the child activates with its parent).

complete.description: dsl 0.24.0 §2: `any` for a `<quest complete="any">` — the quest completes when ANY required objective is done, and every other still-active child fails with `failedBy: superseded`. Omitted for the default `all`.

accept.description: dsl 0.25.0 §5: `external` for a `<quest accept="external">` — the quest is accepted outside the script (a quest board, a menu, a UI): the engine offers it and activates it whenever the player takes it (for an `activate="accept"` child, while the parent is `active`). Omitted by default (only `::accept` accepts it).

cmdQuest.description: <quest> declaration head (dsl 0.2.0 §6.3). Objective completion bodies and <on> arms follow as their own positioned records.

body.description: position of the action body segment.

target.description: dsl 0.24.0 §2: the handler fires only when the same-named occasion is raised for this target. Omitted when unauthored (the handler answers every raise).

cmdOn.description: <on> event-condition-action record (dsl 0.2.0 §4, §6.6): an independent event rule.

id.description: the entry id, unique across the project; also the lineId identity prefix of its body.

target.description: engine-owned id the entry is attached to (`item.rusty_key`, `npc.vesna`); shape-only.

category.description: the lore entry's engine-vocabulary text kind (`note`, `item`, `place`, `codex`, `bark`, …); shape-only. Unrelated to the record `family`.

titleLineId.description: `{entryId}.title`, present only when `title` is authored (the quest `titleLineId` convention).

series.description: groups multi-part text (`scientistLog`). The RESOLVED series (dsl 0.19.0 §2.1): the document-level `series:` when the document declares one, else the entry's own `series=`.

order.description: position within `series`; present only with `series`. The RESOLVED order (dsl 0.19.0 §2.1): the entry's 1-based position among the document's entries under a document-level `series:`, else its own `order=`.

when.description: eligibility: the entry may be presented only while this holds.

body.description: position of the entry's body segment (the `cmdOn.body` convention): it follows this record and runs to the next `entry` or `beat` record or the end of the stream. `set`/`assert`/`retract` records in it apply only on the first read (`entry.<id>.read == false`).

on.description: dsl 0.21.0 §3.2: the occasion this entry answers, which makes it an entry beat (docs/runtime/beats-and-occasions.md). Absent when not authored.

priority.description: dsl 0.21.0 §3.2: the entry beat's authored priority (higher wins). Absent when not authored; the engine reads an absent priority as 0.

once.description: dsl 0.22.0 §7, 0.24.0 §1: the entry beat's repetition policy — `run`: not eligible while `entry.<id>.read` is true; `user`: not eligible once `entry.<id>.everRead` is true; `day` / `slot`: not eligible again until the declared clock's day / slot changes after it was read. Absent when not authored: repeatable, as in 0.21.

share.description: dsl 0.25.0 §2: the shared-spend key, as sceneBeat.share — reading this entry spends every beat of the key, and any of them being presented spends this entry, for the common `once` period. Absent when not authored.

spentBy.description: dsl 0.27.0 §5: the beat (`once: none`) stays eligible until this `@def`-expanded condition holds. Absent when not authored.

advances.description: dsl 0.31.0 §1: clock movement performed when the beat is presented.

cmdEntry.description: <entry> declaration head of a lore artifact (dsl 0.19.0 §7, docs/runtime/lore-entries.md): content the engine looks up rather than plays.

quest.description: id of an accept-driven quest (one with no `start`) in the project; checked by `check-project` (`E-ACCEPT-TARGET`).

applies.description: dsl 0.24.0 §2: `nextRun` for `::accept{… at="nextRun"}` — the acceptance is queued and applies after the next run-start reset. Omitted for an immediate accept.

cmdAccept.description: `::accept{quest}` (dsl 0.21.0 §7a.3): the player accepts an accept-driven quest at this point — the scene-side form of the engine's accept action. The engine activates the quest if its state is `unset` (stamping `activatedAt` as for any activation) and ignores the record otherwise (docs/runtime/quest-lifecycle.md).

id.description: the canonical `<document id>.<beat id>` — the project.index.json beats row id, the `visited()` key, and the lineId identity prefix of the beat's body.

on.description: the occasion this beat answers (the sceneBeat.on shape).

target.description: the beat is a candidate only when the occasion is raised for this target (dotted id). Absent when the beat answers the occasion for any target.

title.description: the label an engine shows for this beat in a `select: all` menu. Absent when not authored.

titleLineId.description: `{id}.title`, present only when `title` is authored (the cmdEntry convention).

when.description: eligibility condition, `@def`-expanded. Absent when not authored.

once.description: repetition policy, as sceneBeat.once: `run` (default), `user`, `none` (source `once=false`), `day` / `slot` (dsl 0.24.0 §1). Spent when the beat is presented.

also.description: as sceneBeat.also (dsl 0.23.0 §3). Absent when not authored.

share.description: dsl 0.25.0 §2: the shared-spend key, as sceneBeat.share. Absent when not authored.

after.description: dsl 0.25.0 §3: the RAW authored `after=` prerequisite — the restricted `visited` / `completed` / `active` grammar of a scene's `after:` — an eligibility conjunct (the beat is eligible only while it and `when` hold). The artifact's `prereqEdges` carries the same text under the beat's `id` as its scenario edge. Absent when not authored.

spentBy.description: dsl 0.27.0 §5: the beat (`once: none`) stays eligible until this `@def`-expanded condition holds. Absent when not authored.

advances.description: dsl 0.31.0 §1: clock movement performed when the beat is presented.

body.description: position of the beat's body segment: it follows this record and runs to the next `entry` or `beat` record or the end of the stream. The body is lowered like a scene section (lines, choices, hubs, match, directives).

cmdBeat.description: A bundle beat's declaration head in a lore artifact (dsl 0.23.0 §4, docs/runtime/beats-and-occasions.md): a scene-like beat written in a lore document. It is the first record of its own addressing unit; the engine presents its body like a scene when the beat wins its occasion.

plugin.description: owning plugin id for a resolved plugin directive; absent for core or unknown directives.

fields.description: resolved directive attrs, typed via the manifest AttrDecls.

effects.description: resolved plugin state-write bindings (IR A12); absent when the directive declares none.

retracts.description: dsl 0.27.0 §4: the facts the call retracts (its directive's declared effects.retracts, @attr substituted; "_" a wildcard), applied after `effects`; absent when none.

asserts.description: dsl 0.27.0 §4: the ground facts the call asserts (its directive's declared effects.asserts, @attr substituted), applied after `retracts`; absent when none.

cmdPlugin.description: Plugin-directive passthrough (Rust `Command::Plugin`), serialized as kind `plugin`. Declared fields and effects are opaque to core. Plugin `stampAttrs` cross-cutting attrs appear as further top-level keys beside `timing`.

command.description: One command record (dsl 0.37.0 §5.3), tagged on `kind` with its `family`. An engine MUST error on an unknown `kind` (version-negotiation policy, top-level description); it MUST ignore unknown FIELDS within a known record.

artifactMeta.description: Kind-polymorphic envelope meta (untagged): SceneMeta when kind==scene, QuestMeta when kind==quest, LoreMeta when kind==lore. The shapes overlap (a bare `{"id": …}` fits all three, since dsl 0.19.0 §2.1 gives quest and lore documents an optional `id`), so this is `anyOf`, not `oneOf`: the top-level allOf pins the exact one by `kind`.

id.description: dsl 0.19.0 §2.1: the lore document's authored `id:` verbatim (same shape as a scene `id:`). The document's ProjectIndex key. Absent when not authored.

series.description: dsl 0.19.0 §2.1 (D-K): the document-level `series:` — every entry of the document belongs to it, ordered by position in the file. Each entry record already carries the resolved `series`/`order`. Absent when not authored.

loreMeta.description: Lore-kind envelope meta (dsl 0.19.0 §7): `id?`, `title?`, `series?`, `contentLang?`, `extra?`, `plugin?` — every field skipped when unauthored, so it MAY serialize as {}. Present when `kind` == "lore".

indexEntry.description: One row of `project.index.json` `entries` (dsl 0.19.0 §7; `lute compile --all`): every `<entry>` in the project, documents in path order, entries in document order within each. The index itself is not an artifact; this row shape is published here for engines that read it. `entries` is omitted from the index when the project has no lore.

id.description: the scene's canonical id (sceneMeta.id) for a scene beat, the entry id for an entry beat, the canonical `<document id>.<beat id>` for a bundle beat (dsl 0.23.0 §4).

once.description: the beat's repetition policy: always present on a scene or bundle row; on an entry row the authored `once` (`run`/`user`, dsl 0.22.0 §7; `day`/`slot`, dsl 0.24.0 §1), absent = repeatable.

spentBy.description: dsl 0.27.0 §5: the beat's `spentBy` condition after `@def` expansion (raw CEL). Absent when not authored.

when.description: dsl 0.23.0 §1: the beat's condition after `@def` expansion (raw CEL). Absent when not authored.

title.description: dsl 0.23.0 §11: the scene's `title:`, or the entry's or bundle beat's `title=` — enough to label a `select: all` menu row. Absent when not authored.

share.description: dsl 0.25.0 §2: the beat's shared-spend key — every row of one key is spent when any of them is presented (an entry: read). Absent when not authored.

indexBeat.description: One row of `project.index.json` `beats` (dsl 0.21.0 §8; `lute compile --all`): every scene, entry and bundle beat in the project, documents in path order, declaration order within each. Row order is the selection tiebreak after priority (docs/runtime/beats-and-occasions.md). `beats` is omitted from the index when the project has no beats.

section.description: one-based document position of the section; matches the first segment of a record `position`.

heading.description: the verbatim `## ` heading text, the `{#id}` suffix excluded (empty when the section has only an id).

id.description: dsl 0.37.0 §3.1: the authored stable section id (`## Heading {#id}`), unique within the document. Omitted when unauthored.

sectionEntry.description: dsl 0.37.0 §5.3: one authored document section. Purely descriptive — control flow never references it.

day.description: the day path — an `int` state path declared `owner: engine` (else `E-CLOCK-DECL`). Day 1 is the first day.

slot.description: the slot path — an enum state path declared `owner: engine`. Absent on a day-granular clock (every day is one slot).

slots.description: the slot order within a day; exactly the slot enum's members, each once. Present exactly when `slot` is.

oneOf.description: one occasion, raised after every advance where the clock stops (the map form's `slot`).

slot.description: raised once after every advance, where the clock stops.

dayStart.description: raised at every midnight an advance crosses, after it — at the next day's first slot.

dayEnd.description: raised at every midnight an advance crosses, before it — at the day's last slot, the day not yet advanced.

raise.description: the occasions the engine raises as the clock advances, verbatim as declared. Absent when not declared.

raiseAtStart.description: dsl 0.28.0: the engine raises the clock's slot occasion (the string form, or the map's `slot`) and the map's `dayStart` itself at the run's first position, where no advance stops. Omitted when `false` (the default): nothing is raised where the run starts, and `dayStart` is never raised on its day.

first.description: the 0-based weekday index of day 1 (below `length`); always serialized, `0` when not declared.

labels.description: one display label per weekday, in weekday order (exactly `length` of them). Omitted when not declared.

week.description: the optional week. Absent when not declared.

slot.description: the last slot — one of `slots`; omitted means the day's last slot (always omitted on a day-granular clock).

last.description: dsl 0.27.0 §4 (T2-5): a finite clock's last position, verbatim as declared. Absent when not declared (the clock never ends).

days.description: dsl 0.27.0 §4: `days: N`, verbatim — short for `last: { day: N }` (the last slot of day N). Never together with `last`; absent when not declared.

clockDecl.description: dsl 0.24.0 §1: the project's declared clock, verbatim from the schema's `clock:` block. Carried on the artifact root and on `project.index.json` (`lute compile --all`) as `clock`. The engine derives the reserved read-only paths from it — `clock.index` = `(day - 1) * len(slots) + slotIndex` (`day - 1` without slots; monotone), `clock.weekday` = `(week.first + day - 1) mod week.length`, `clock.weekdayLabel` = `week.labels[clock.weekday]` — none of which is a `state` row, and spends `once: day|slot` beats by it. An advance moves the clock forward only (the last slot wraps to the first slot of the next day), settles quests and raises `raise` (`dayEnd` / `dayStart` at each midnight it crosses, `slot` where it stops) when declared. dsl 0.27.0 §4: a finite clock (`last` / `days`) stops at its last position — an advance whose destination lies past it walks there (raising `dayEnd` / `dayStart` at each midnight it crosses on the way), raises the last day's `dayEnd` (never `slot`) and ends the clock; any later advance is the usage error `E-CLOCK-END` until a new run starts the clock over.

indexOccasion.description: The serializable capability occasion shape in project.index.json, without description or raisedWhen.

indexStateDomain.description: A closed state member domain, keyed by state path in project.index.json.

projectIndex.description: The optional capability unions carried by project.index.json.
